_readme: Machine-readable run blocks for Banco, keyed by beat id. The prompt TEXT is never here - it lives in demo-prompts.json, vendored from the deck (docs/adr/0001). This file holds only what a program needs in order to execute a beat: how many panes, which kind of model source each pane wants, the sampling parameters the room must see, and which file is pasted in. Merged over the demo database at load time by app/server/runs.py, so the vendored copy stays byte-identical to its pin. See docs/adr/0003.
_roles_note: A pane asks for a ROLE, never a named provider. 'primary' and 'secondary' are two different API providers; 'local' is Ollama. The profile chosen at first run binds roles to concrete providers, which is what lets a missing source degrade a beat to replay instead of removing it (PROJECT.md, Configuration model). A run block that named 'anthropic' would break the offline profile and could not degrade.
_temperature_note: Temperature is stated explicitly on every pane because the room has to see it - that is objective 2, and it is why m1-p3 was a dead branch on consumer products. The value is data, not code: change it here.

m1-p1.teaches: Sampling variance, and that fields absent from the source get filled anyway.
m1-p1._panes_note: Two samples from each of two sources, because this beat teaches two things at once: the same model disagrees with itself (panes 0 vs 1, 2 vs 3), and two models disagree with each other (A vs B). PROJECT.md records D1 as only 'partly' local-capable for exactly this reason - sampling works with one source, cross-source disagreement does not.

m1-p2.teaches: Asked for its source, the model either admits it inferred the value or points at a passage that is not there.
m1-p2._continues_note: The deck says 'the same chat, right after'. Each pane carries its own m1-p1 exchange forward as conversation history, so pane 2 is asked about what pane 2 wrote. Restarting the conversation here would destroy the beat: there would be no prior entry to interrogate.
